2607.08400.title: TRACE: A Two-Channel Robust Attribution Watermark via Complementary Embeddings for LLM-Agent Trajectories
2607.08400.paper_summary: LLM agents reach users through resellers, who may rebrand a developer's agent or substitute a cheaper model. When provenance is disputed, attribution rests on the trajectory log (the record of tool calls, observations, and executed actions, not the model's reasoning), which the reseller stores and processes to meter usage. A watermark must therefore survive an adversary with full read/write access to the very evidence it is detected from; existing agent watermarks do not, as their attribution is read straight off that log. We present TRACE, to our knowledge the first agent watermark that is distortion-free in its action choices, self-synchronizing under deletion, and unconditionally invariant under rewriting. Deletion desynchronizes a position-derived key and rewriting alters content, so a deletion-robust key must come from content and a rewrite-robust key from position, and no single key serves both. A trajectory, however, has room for two watermarks. TRACE superposes a selection channel that sets which action is chosen, keyed on local content with a distortion-free sampler, so the agent's distribution is provably unchanged and detection resynchronizes after deletions, and a tally channel that sets how many records each decision group holds, keyed on the log's skeleton alone, which no rewriting can touch. We prove this behavioral watermark's signal is bought with decision entropy, each decision paying at least half its entropy and deterministic decisions nothing, and that erasing both channels forces the reseller to corrupt the trajectories it resells. On ToolBench and ALFWorld, TRACE matches the unwatermarked agent's success rate while its selection channel reaches detection scores near z = 100 on long-horizon trajectories, stays detectable under 70% step deletion, and keeps a tally channel exactly unchanged under LLM rewriting of any strength.
2607.08400.paper_summary_zh: LLM 代理透過轉售商接觸用戶，轉售商可能會重新品牌開發者的代理或替換為更便宜的模型。當來源受到質疑時，歸屬權依賴於軌跡日誌（工具調用、觀察和執行行動的記錄，而非模型的推理），轉售商存儲並處理該日誌以計量使用量。因此，水印必須能夠抵抗擁有完全讀寫權限的對手，這些對手可以接觸到檢測所依賴的證據；現有的代理水印無法做到這一點，因為它們的歸屬權是直接從該日誌中讀取的。我們提出了 TRACE，據我們所知，這是第一個在行動選擇上無失真的代理水印，能在刪除下自我同步，並在重寫下無條件不變。刪除會使基於位置的密鑰不同步，而重寫會改變內容，因此一個抗刪除的密鑰必須來自內容，而一個抗重寫的密鑰必須來自位置，且沒有單一的密鑰能同時滿足兩者。然而，一條軌跡有空間容納兩個水印。TRACE 超疊了一個選擇通道，設置選擇哪個行動，基於本地內容使用無失真的抽樣器，因此代理的分佈是可證明不變的，並且在刪除後檢測會重新同步，還有一個計數通道，設置每個決策組持有的記錄數量，僅基於日誌的骨架，這是任何重寫都無法觸及的。我們證明這個行為水印的信號是以決策熵為代價的，每個決策至少支付其熵的一半，而確定性決策則不支付任何費用，並且刪除這兩個通道會迫使轉售商損壞其轉售的軌跡。在 ToolBench 和 ALFWorld 上，TRACE 的成功率與未加水印的代理相匹配，而其選擇通道在長期軌跡上達到接近 z = 100 的檢測分數，並在 70% 步驟刪除下保持可檢測性，且在任何強度的 LLM 重寫下計數通道保持完全不變。
